message:
proofbundle 6.4.0

Feature release 6.4.0. See CHANGELOG.md and the release notes for release information. RESTRISIKO_640.md contains the existing risk record for this version; the four additional findings from the deep gate are listed below and remain open in this release.

THE DEEP GATE FOR THIS RELEASE DID NOT PASS. This tag records the owner's decision to release with the findings listed below. The candidate is e636b5da1b615f2ca1596229193fdc6b97cc3acf, the head of main after pull request 427. The full test suite referenced by the pre-tag receipt, the full mutation run, a 300-second short soak and the Python–Rust differential were run at the candidate commit. The tagged commit is the evidence commit on the candidate; it changes only the pre-tag receipt, the short soak record and the differential record, and a build at it gives the same sdist and wheel bytes as at the candidate. A 24 hour soak started at the candidate on 2026-10-27 at 18:53 UTC and ends no earlier than 2026-10-28 at 18:53 UTC; it is not signed and not in the tree, and its result is reported separately.

At the tagged commit, with the candidate sdist and wheel in place, the audit candidate matrix measures 33 of 34 checks: 29 PASS and 4 FAIL. C6.2, C6.3 and C8.2 FAIL because the signed short soak and the signed differential carry the deep gate verdict REFUTED_IN_ITERATION_1, which is not a pass. C10.2 FAILS because the 6.4.0 readiness slot is not filled; it is an informative cell. EXT.1, the independent external audit, is not measured, and audit_candidate_ready is false. Do not read this tag as a gate that was passed.

Findings register: audit_artifacts/findings_register_361.json

Known limitations of this release.

Deep gate for this release: REFUTED_IN_ITERATION_1. A limited adversarial review used one read-only lens on a tree whose src/ is recorded as unchanged at candidate e636b5da1b615f2ca1596229193fdc6b97cc3acf; the second model family and a second iteration did not run. The changes from that candidate to this release leave the verifier code unchanged. The review confirmed one refutation of a pre-registered target and recorded two further, contested refutations. A fourth finding concerned a misleading diagnostic outside those targets. This release has no WITHSTANDS verdict. The four findings remain open in this release; follow-up work is planned after the tag.

The trace record reader (proofbundle.adapters.trace_record) builds one path string per member that carries all of its ancestors. A measured 64,301-byte input needed about 120 MB of memory, and under a 600 MiB address-space limit verify_trace_record raised an uncaught MemoryError before any signature was checked. An input-size limit alone is not an established mitigation. Until this is fixed, do not process untrusted records in a shared or critical process. If such processing is necessary, isolate it in a worker with enforced memory and time limits, and treat an exception or worker termination as a failed verification, never as acceptance.

verify_statement_signature returns ('confirmed', True) for a statement with the unknown critical header crit: [999], while verify_transparent_statement reports the same bytes as outside_profile. Do not treat the signature-only result as confirmation that a statement satisfies the profile. For Transparent Statements, use verify_transparent_statement with the relying party's trust configuration and require a successful verification result. The review recorded this as a contested refutation because the signature-only API has a narrower documented scope.

loads_reject_duplicate_keys, documented as a producer-side reader, still accepts NaN, positive and negative Infinity, 1e400, integers beyond 2^53 - 1, a byte order mark, UTF-16 and lone surrogates. The same behavior was observed in 6.3.1. Do not use this function alone to validate untrusted input or to establish conformance to RFC 8785. Do not infer stricter behavior for this producer-side reader from claims about other parsing entry points. The review recorded this as a contested refutation because of the function's documented producer-side scope.

proofbundle verify-trace can print "POLICY: NOT_EVALUATED (no relying-party expectation supplied)" even when --nonce was supplied but was not evaluated. The measured exit code is correctly 1. Treat this result as a failed verification; do not interpret the diagnostic as evidence that no expectation was supplied or that the supplied nonce was checked.

The deep gate verdict is REFUTED_IN_ITERATION_1, not WITHSTANDS. The release decision record states that this leaves the audit-candidate matrix cells C6.2 and C8.2 red. C6.3 is red for the same cause, because it reads the same short soak record with the same gate line. This is not a passing matrix result, and it does not establish that the readiness artifacts passed the provenance or freshness checks of the matrix. At the tagged commit, the recorded pre-upload comparison exited with code 0 and reported: "OK: the tag run built the signed candidate pair". This result is separate from the failed matrix checks and is not evidence that the matrix's provenance, freshness or gate-line requirements passed.
